QF.id: I Codes of Conduct and Investor Protection_17

question.text: An investor can verify their trade details through:

answer.text: Contract notes from the broker and UCC/PAN-linked client trade records
Only the newspaper the next day
Only by visiting the exchange physically

explanation.text: The Logic: Pages 143 and 220 of the NISM Series I Currency Derivatives workbook (December 2025) confirm that contract notes from the broker are the official record of trades, and page 240 confirms that client trades are mapped to the client's UCC and PAN before being routed to the exchange. Together, these provide source-backed verification of an investor's trade details. The Trap: Verbal confirmations, newspaper listings, and physical exchange visits are not the recognised verification mechanisms; written/electronic records issued by the broker and the UCC/PAN-linked records are. Note: The earlier reference to "trade verification on an exchange website" was not found in the pages checked (129-130, 143, 147, 220, 224, 240) and has been removed.
